label: Stern gland greaser
caption: In the stern locker, looking down at the weed hatch. The green circle marks the greaser to the right of the hatch cover - twist it clockwise after a day's cruising until the dripping in the back bedroom stops.
notes: Same photograph as figure 8, annotated differently. Here the circle is on the greaser; in figure 8 it is on the weed hatch cover.

label: Raw water strainers and the alternative intake lever
caption: Two clear-topped raw water strainers side by side on the engine room bulkhead, with the white lever valve for the alternative intake at the bottom left. Unscrew the tops to empty the plastic filters, keeping the black seals.

label: Side intake valve between the tanks
caption: The second of the two valves to switch when the rear intakes are blocked, circled in green: a lever valve on the pipework between the tanks on the starboard side, above the water pumps and the blue accumulators.

label: Main engine throttle and gear lever
caption: The chrome throttle/gear lever on the wheelhouse console, with a green arrow pointing to it. Pull it out to the right to disengage the gearbox and put her in neutral before starting.

label: Main engine start panel (Perkins Sabre)
caption: The black Perkins Sabre instrument panel: gauges and tachometer, with the HEAT and ON toggle switches at the right and the STOP button below them. Switch ON, hold HEAT up a few seconds, then pull HEAT towards you to crank.

label: Rudder angle indicator
caption: The Vetus RUDDER gauge on the wheelhouse console, reading zero with the needle straight up - rudder centred. The red tape on the steering wheel should be at the top to match.

label: Bow thruster control
caption: The Vetus BOW-THRUSTER panel: a green ON button with ON/OFF markings and the sideways rocker joystick below. For moving the bow at slow speed, not useful at cruising speed.

label: Weed hatch in the stern locker
caption: The same stern locker as figure 1, with the green circle now around the weed hatch cover itself. Open it to reach the propeller - engine off first.
notes: Same photograph as figure 1, annotated differently.

label: Long fender against mooring posts
caption: A long black ladder-style fender hung vertically between Becky's hull and a timber mooring post, sitting parallel to the water and covering the outermost part of the hull. These are stored in the bow locker.

label: Main electrical distribution panel
caption: The glass-fronted panel in the wheelhouse. Left side is D.C. POWER with amps/volts meters and labelled breakers; right side is A.C. POWER with volts, warning lamps, the INVERTER and SHIP/SHORE selectors, and rocker switches for SHORE and GEN. This is where the three loops are switched on and off.

label: Fridge switch
caption: The local switch on the bulkhead directly above the fridge in the galley. Switch it off when leaving Becky off power.
notes: Not labelled in the photograph; identified from its position and the surrounding text. The freezer switch in figure 12 is explicitly labelled.

label: Freezer switch (labelled FREEZER)
caption: A rocker switch with an engraved FREEZER label, above a switched 13 A socket with the freezer plugged in. Switch it off when leaving Becky off power.

label: Inverter/charger switch (Victron Phoenix MultiPlus)
caption: The blue Victron Phoenix MultiPlus 24/3000/70 inverter/charger mounted in the engine room, with the green circle around its on / off / charger-only switch. Leave it on while using the boat; turn it off only when leaving her unattended off grid. An MPPT solar charge controller is on the panel to its right.

label: Generator control panel (Vetus)
caption: The small Vetus generator panel with warning lamps for temperature, oil, coolant and battery, and four buttons along the bottom: green ON, a heat/glow-coil button, START and STOP. Press On, then Heat, then Start.

label: Heating and hot water controller (Eberspacher timer)
caption: The Eberspacher 7-day timer on the bulkhead, showing the clock. The green circle is around the heat button at the bottom right that turns the heating and hot water on and off. After switching off it takes about 90 seconds for the heater to shut down.

label: Immersion heater timer and boost dial (Grasslin ECOsave)
caption: The Grasslin ECOsave immersion timer with its clock dial on the left and ON/OFF switch in the middle. The green circle marks the BOOST TIME dial - 15, 30, 60 or 120 minutes; choose the time and push the dial in. The generator needs to be running.

label: Bathroom light and extractor fan switch
caption: The round stainless ceiling light in the bathroom, with the green circle around the small black push switch on the deckhead beside it that works the light and extractor fan. The extractor grille is visible below.

label: Shower drain pump switch
caption: A small black push switch circled in green on the dark blue panel at the base of the bathroom unit. The shower plug hole is below the waterline, so this pump has to be running to drain it.

label: Toilet FILL and FLUSH buttons (Tecma)
caption: The black Tecma control plate beside the toilet with two white buttons, FILL above and FLUSH below, and a green indicator lamp between them.

label: Tank level gauges
caption: Three round gauges stacked on the pale green bulkhead by the stairs into the wheelhouse, each reading empty to 4/4. The middle is marked WATER and the bottom WASTE. The manual notes the gauges read conservatively.
notes: The top gauge's label is not legible in the photograph; by elimination it is the fuel gauge, but that is inferred rather than read.

label: Deck filler key (Lee Sanitation)
caption: The white T-shaped Lee Sanitation deck-plate key, with four pegs along the crossbar that engage the filler cap. Stored in the wheelhouse cupboard and used for the water, diesel and pump-out caps.

label: Water deck filler being opened
caption: The black deck plate cast with WATER on the foredeck, with the Lee Sanitation key engaged in it to twist the inner cap out.

label: Blue drinking-water hose in the water filler
caption: The open WATER deck filler with a blue hose feeding into it. Blue hoses are for drinking water only - green are for river water and washing out the waste tanks. It bangs when nearly full and overflows near the starboard bow.

label: Pump-out deck fitting, closed
caption: The closed black pump-out deck plate set into the starboard side deck, level with the gunwale and the river beyond.

label: Pump-out deck fitting being opened
caption: The same starboard deck plate, cast PUMP OUT, with the Lee Sanitation key engaged in the inner cap to open it for a service-point suction hose.

label: Pump switches: DIESEL TRANSFER, WASTE and DECK WASH
caption: Three black push switches in a row on the pale green bulkhead with engraved brass labels: DIESEL TRANSFER PUMP, WASTE PUMP and DECK WASH PUMP. The waste pump is Becky's own pump-out for service points that have no suction; the diesel transfer pump moves fuel from the main engine tank to the leisure tank.

label: Deck wash outlet and hose connector
caption: A hex-topped standpipe in the corner of the deck with a beige quick-release hose connector lying beside it. Use the green hoses from the bow locker on this - it draws river water.

label: Diesel deck filler cap
caption: The black diesel deck plate with a square drive socket in the centre, and its curved chrome-edged nameplate reading DIESEL alongside. This is the main engine tank on the port side.

label: The solid fuel stove (Morso Squirrel)
caption: The black cast-iron Morso Squirrel stove in its hearth beside the stairs, with a heat-powered fan on the top plate. Leave the top vent open to keep the glass clear and regulate the fire on the bottom vent.

label: Galvanised bin for hot coals and ash
caption: A lidded galvanised steel bin standing on the deck, used to put potentially hot coals and ash into.

label: The BW key for river utilities
caption: A brass key and a key marked BW on a cork ball float. The BW key opens the utilities on the river - waste disposal, water points and locks. All the keys live in the cupboard in the rear bedroom.

label: Emergency cassette toilet in the bow hatch
caption: A white portable cassette toilet sitting in the red external storage hatch in the bow, with hoses coiled below it. It empties via a cassette.

label: Portable emergency bilge pump
caption: A white portable submersible pump with a green hose attached and its mains lead coiled around it, stored in the engine room. The backup for the main bilge pump, or for water in a part of the boat the main pump does not reach.

label: Electrical system overview diagram
caption: A block diagram of Becky's electrical system. Generator, Shore Power, Solar Power and Main Engine feed in on the left; the Main Engine goes through a Diode Split Charger (28 A max) to the main engine starter batteries; Generator and Shore feed an Inverter/Charger (40 A max) and the generator starter battery; the Leisure Batteries sit in the middle and supply a second Inverter/Charger to the AC 240V loop (hob, immersion heater, washing machine, normal sockets) and the DC 12V and 24V loops (lights, instrument panel, pumps, radio, round plug sockets).
